items.finding: The review describes low-level data fusion as the simplest way to combine inputs by rearranging variables from different sources into a new data matrix.
items.how_it_applies: This could inform the pilot by treating low-level fusion as a simple starting architecture for synchronised NIR and Raman data, but it does not establish that a fused model will outperform the best single method.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a general PAT data-fusion review, not a tablet feed-frame study; it gives no evidence on synchronised NIR/Raman spectra, block scaling, or held-out run comparison for this blend.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E02 ¶31

items.finding: The review states that before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate each dataset's contribution to the model and its complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: This supports including per-method diagnostics and checking whether Raman adds useful information beyond NIR before keeping a fused model in the pilot assessment.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: This is a general review statement, not a tablet feed-frame experiment; it does not show that NIR and Raman are complementary for this powder blend or that fusion will improve performance.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
